title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. K is a field, L/K a function field (finitely generated), and \bar L an algebraic closure of L. Following Grothendieck's notation, E^{\bar L}_L is the absolute Galois group Gal(\bar L/L), viewed as an extension of Gal(\bar K/K) by the 'geometric' part \Pi^{\bar L}_{L/K}. For a regular model Y of L/K, E^{\bar L}_Y is the arithmetic fundamental group \pi_1(Y,\bar\eta) with base point given by \bar L.

The previous page states the known fact that, for a proper regular model X, E^{\bar L}_X is a quotient of E^{\bar L}_L that does not depend on X. This page names that quotient:
- It is the 'universally unramified' part of E^{\bar L}_L. I read the handwriting as 'universellement non ramifiée'; the machine reading is 'donnée'.
- Grothendieck denotes it E_{\mathbf L} (bold L).
- It classifies the finite étale L-schemes that 'compactify', i.e. extend to finite étale covers, over every proper regular model of L/K, projective or not.

Next, let U be any regular model. It embeds as an open set in a proper regular X. This uses Nagata compactification followed by resolution of singularities, so implicitly characteristic 0 or low dimension. The result is the chain of surjections (21):
  E_L → E_U → E_X = E_{\mathbf L}.

Write U = X \ Z (22), where Z is closed in X. Let D_i be the codimension-1 components of Z and x_i their generic points. In E_U one has decomposition and inertia groups D_{x'_i} ⊃ I_{x'_i}. These depend on a choice of a point x'_i over x_i in the normalization of X in \bar L.

The next page completes the statement (23): E_X ≅ E_U / (normal subgroup generated by the I_{x_i}). This is the Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus (SGA1 X 3.1–3.4; SGA2 X). Points of Z of codimension ≥ 2 play no role because X is regular. It then records E_L = lim_U E_U (24) and the corresponding statement for the geometric parts \Pi (25).

Purpose: to set up a 'birational' description of the arithmetic fundamental group of a function field. Gal(\bar L/L) is presented as the projective limit of the \pi_1 of its regular models, with the unramified quotient \pi_1(X) as the birational invariant at the bottom. The next page passes to local analysis at a codimension-1 point, i.e. the DVR of a divisor, to describe the inertia groups. This is groundwork for the anabelian/birational programme of the Longue Marche.
errors: Embedding an arbitrary regular model U into a proper *regular* X requires resolution of singularities. This is fine in characteristic 0 (Hironaka) or in dimension ≤ 2 (≤ 3 in many cases), but is not known in general in positive characteristic. Grothendieck states it without qualification ('il se plonge dans un X').

Independence of E_X from the proper regular model X (the birational invariance of \pi_1) also relies on purity plus the existence of common regular proper dominating models. This again implicitly needs resolution in positive characteristic, unless one argues via valuations/purity directly.
Superscripts are written inconsistently on the page: E^L_U should read E^{\bar L}_U. This is notational, not mathematical.

ideas.what: The quotient of Gal(\bar L/L) classifying finite étale L-algebras that extend to étale covers on every proper regular model: the birationally invariant 'unramified' fundamental group E_{\mathbf L} = \pi_1(X)
ideas.modern_name: Birational invariance of \pi_1 of smooth proper varieties; unramified quotient of the absolute Galois group of a function field
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 X 3.4), building on Zariski–Nagata purity

ideas.what: Surjections Gal(\bar L/L) → \pi_1(U) → \pi_1(X) for an open regular U in a proper regular X
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of \pi_1 for dominant maps and open immersions of normal schemes

ideas.what: Kernel of \pi_1(U) → \pi_1(X) as the normal closure of the inertia groups at generic points of the boundary divisors (completed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus; inertia generation of the kernel
ideas.usually_credited_to: Zariski, Nagata; Grothendieck (SGA1 X, SGA2 X)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. X 3.1–3.4; SGA2 Exp. X

ideas.what: Decomposition and inertia groups at codimension-1 points, dependent on a choice of point over x_i in the normalization of X in \bar L
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hilbert; Grothendieck–Murre for the tame case)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V, XIII; Grothendieck–Murre LNM 208

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard set-up: the birational invariance of \pi_1 of proper regular models, purity, and the inertia description of the kernel, all in SGA1/SGA2. Its only interest is as groundwork for the birational-anabelian programme of the Longue Marche. It contains no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: 'partie "universellement donnée"' is more plausibly 'partie "universellement non ramifiée"', which matches the mathematical meaning.
'qui sont "non compactifiables" sur tout modèle local régulier (groupe ou non)' should read approximately 'qui se "compactifient" sur tout modèle propre régulier (projectif ou non)'.
The crossed-out phrase is approximately '[-qui couvre les buts-] \mathcal{E}^{\bar L}_{L/K} (extensions de K)'; the superscript is \bar L.
In (21), E^{L}_{L} and E^{L}_{U} should be E^{\bar L}_L and E^{\bar L}_U; the right-hand side is E^{\bar L}_{\mathbf L} with a bold L.
'N_{x'_i}' is likely a script \mathcal{D}_{x'_i} (decomposition group), paired with the inertia group \mathbf{I}_{x'_i}.
'Z partie fermée de X - réunion des D_i' should probably read 'Z partie fermée de X, D_i ses composantes de codim 1, x_i les pts génériques des D_i'.
The crossed word before (22) is 'Etat' or similar; 'On aura' is correct.
